title: 8 Lee Se-young K-dramas to revisit during “The Remarried Empress” - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong

 By Tom Kao November 16, 2026 Lee Se-young makes Rashta easy to hate in Disney+’s "The Remarried Empress." A runaway slave who becomes Emperor Sovieshu’s (Ju Ji-hoon) mistress, Rashta upends his marriage to Empress Navier (Shin Min-a). Lee can make her sound so sweet and unassuming that you’re left wondering how much of it is an act. If Rashta has you hooked on palace politics, there’s more of Lee to revisit, starting with a court lady who has her own ideas about what a royal romance is worth. Here are eight of her K-dramas to watch between episodes 
 The Red Sleeve (2021)
 If palace life is what drew you to The Remarried Empress , start with The Red Sleeve . Set in 18th-century Joseon, it follows Seong Deok-im (Lee), a quick-witted court lady who catches the eye of Crown Prince Yi San (Lee Jun-ho), the future King Jeongjo. The two grow closer as he fights to secure his claim to the throne, but she turns him down when he asks her to become his consort. Watch how at ease Lee is around Deok-im’s friends, and you’ll see why that offer gives her pause.
 The Crowned Clown (2019)
 For more palace intrigue, try The Crowned Clown , where a queen finds herself warming to a man she thinks she already knows. When King Yi Heon fears for his life, a travelling clown named Ha-seon takes his place. Yeo Jin-goo plays both men, while Lee plays Queen Yoo So-woon, who’s puzzled by her husband’s sudden kindness. As Ha-seon falls for her, even an ordinary conversation feels like a chance for him to slip up. Lee lets the queen’s affection build slowly enough to keep you watching for her next reaction.
 What Comes After Love (2024)
 Save What Comes After Love for a night when you’re in the mood for a quiet romance that lingers. Choi Hong (Lee) falls for aspiring writer Jungo Aoki (Kentaro Sakaguchi) while studying in Japan. Five years after their breakup, he turns up in Korea to promote a novel about their relationship, just as she’s settled into a job at her father’s publishing company. The flashbacks make the reunion sting, especially when you watch Lee put on a polite smile for someone Hong once felt completely at ease with.

 The Story of Park’s Marriage Contract (2023)
 If you like your period romances with a little chaos, The Story of Park’s Marriage Contract is an easy pick. Park Yeon-woo (Lee) loses her husband on their wedding night in Joseon, gets thrown down a well and surfaces in a swimming pool in modern-day Seoul. The man who pulls her out, Kang Tae-ha (Bae In-hyuk), looks exactly like her late husband and needs a stand-in bride. Lee is especially fun to watch once Yeon-woo starts bringing her own ideas about marriage to a deal meant to last a day.
 The Law Cafe (2022)
 In the mood for a rom-com with plenty of bickering? The Law Cafe pairs Lee with Lee Seung-gi as two old friends who can turn a simple chat into an argument. She plays Kim Yu-ri, a lawyer who opens a café where a cup of coffee comes with legal advice. He’s Kim Jeong-ho, her new landlord and a former prosecutor who’s liked her since high school. The cases give them plenty to argue about, and Lee is funniest when Yu-ri digs in her heels and dares him to disagree.
 Kairos (2020)
 For a thriller that’ll have you watching the clock, put on Kairos . At 10:33 each night, Han Ae-ri (Lee) gets one minute on the phone with Kim Seo-jin (Shin Sung-rok), who’s living a month in her future. He needs her help preventing his daughter’s kidnapping, while she’s trying to find her mother, who vanished from hospital. The deadline makes every pause count, and you can hear in Lee’s voice how quickly a call from a stranger goes from something Ae-ri can barely believe to something she can’t afford to miss.
 Doctor John (2019)
 If you like a medical drama that gives you a mystery to puzzle over, give Doctor John a go. Kang Si-young (Lee) first meets anaesthesiologist Cha Yo-han (Ji Sung) while working at the prison where he’s serving time. They later join the same hospital team, taking on cases of unexplained pain that have stumped other doctors. Yo-han’s past raises difficult questions about how far a doctor should go to relieve suffering, and Lee gives the cases a human touch by showing how carefully Si-young listens to her patients.
 Motel California (2025)
 For a small-town romance with some history behind it, end with Motel California . Ji Gang-hee (Lee) leaves her father’s countryside motel for Seoul, where she builds a career in interior design. A renovation project brings her back 12 years later, and she runs into her first love, Cheon Yeon-soo (Na In-woo), now the local vet. Gang-hee wants to keep the visit quiet, which takes some doing in a town that remembers them both. There’s a warmth in Lee’s performance whenever the two slip into conversation like old friends.
